questions.title: Solution with excess hydroxyl ions
questions.question: Which of the following is a solution that contains hydroxyl ions in excess of hydrogen ions?

explanations.A: Incorrect. An acidic solution has hydrogen-ion concentration in excess of hydroxyl-ion concentration, the reverse of what the question describes.
explanations.B: Correct. A basic solution has pH above 7, with hydrogen-ion concentration below hydroxyl-ion concentration -- exactly the hydroxyl-in-excess state the question describes. This is a general-chemistry classification, distinct from (though related to) the human body's own tightly regulated blood pH set-point of 7.35-7.45.
explanations.C: Incorrect. "Hypotonic" describes a solution's relative solute concentration compared to another solution (relevant to osmosis), not its hydrogen/hydroxyl ion balance.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A neutral solution has equal hydrogen-ion and hydroxyl-ion concentrations, not an excess of either.

questions.learning_objective: Classify a solution as basic from an excess of hydroxyl over hydrogen ions.

questions.title: Acid-base consequence of severe exercise
questions.question: Severe muscle exercise usually leads to which of the following?

explanations.A: Correct. Severe muscular exercise outpaces oxidative metabolism's oxygen supply, so muscle shifts to anaerobic glycolysis and produces lactic acid faster than it can be buffered or cleared. This fixed (non-volatile) acid load drops blood pH by a metabolic, not respiratory, route -- the raised breathing rate seen during exercise is the compensatory response to this acid load, not its cause.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Respiratory acidosis results from CO2 retention (inadequate ventilation), which is the opposite of what happens during exercise, when ventilation increases.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Metabolic alkalosis results from a base excess or acid loss (such as prolonged vomiting), not from the acid-producing anaerobic metabolism of exercise.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Respiratory alkalosis results from hyperventilation blowing off too much CO2 relative to the body's acid production, which is not the primary process during severe exercise.

questions.learning_objective: Classify exercise-induced acidosis as metabolic (from lactic acid accumulation), not respiratory.

questions.title: Identifying the branched-chain amino acid
questions.question: Which of the following is a branched amino acid?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Methionine is a sulfur-containing essential amino acid, not one of the branched-chain group.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Proline is a cyclic (imino) amino acid, structurally distinct from the branched-chain group.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Tyrosine is an aromatic amino acid, made from phenylalanine, not one of the branched-chain group.
explanations.D: Correct. Valine, leucine and isoleucine are the branched-chain amino acids, named for the branch point in their aliphatic side chains. Threonine is a common distractor precisely because it is not one of the three despite sometimes being grouped with them by students. All three branched-chain amino acids are essential, meaning the body cannot synthesise them and they must come from the diet.

questions.learning_objective: Identify valine as a branched-chain amino acid.

questions.title: Amino-acid composition of glutathione
questions.question: Which group of amino acids contribute to the structure of glutathione?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Glycine is a genuine component of glutathione, but alanine and tryptophan are not — this combination substitutes two wrong residues.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Neither histidine nor proline are components of glutathione; only the correct answer's three residues are.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Aspartic acid and ornithine are not components of glutathione, though glutamic acid is.
explanations.D: Correct. Glutathione is the tripeptide glutamate-cysteine-glycine. Its biologically active group is the sulfhydryl (-SH) contributed by the cysteine residue, which is oxidised in its redox reactions. This antioxidant role is why glutathione is central to protecting cells against oxidative and toxic damage.

questions.title: Normal blood pH range
questions.question: What is the normal pH range of human blood?

explanations.A: Incorrect. 6.85-7.0 is well below the normal range and would represent severe acidaemia incompatible with the stated "normal" range.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 7.0-7.25 is also below the normal range, representing significant acidaemia.
explanations.C: Correct. Human arterial blood pH is tightly regulated within 7.35-7.45 by the bicarbonate buffer system together with respiratory and renal compensation. A value below 7.35 is acidaemia; above 7.45 is alkalaemia.
explanations.D: Incorrect. 7.55-7.75 is above the normal range and would represent significant alkalaemia.

questions.learning_objective: State the normal arterial blood pH range as 7.35-7.45.

questions.title: Direction of water movement in osmosis
questions.question: Solution A is more concentrated than solution B, and a semi-permeable membrane separates them. Which of the following is correct about this condition?

options.A: Water will pass from solution A to solution B by osmosis
options.B: Water will pass from solution B to solution A by osmosis
options.C: Molecules will pass from solution A to solution B by active transport
options.D: Molecules will pass from solution B to solution A passively

explanations.A: Incorrect. Osmosis moves water toward the more concentrated (higher-solute) side, not away from it, so water does not move from A (more concentrated) to B.
explanations.B: Correct. Osmosis is the movement of solvent (water) across a semipermeable membrane toward the side with the higher solute concentration, diluting it and equalising the concentration gradient. Since solution A is more concentrated, water moves from the less concentrated solution B into A.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The scenario describes a semipermeable membrane, which is defined by letting water (and not the solute) cross — it does not describe active transport of solute molecules, which requires a specific carrier and energy input.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The question specifies a semipermeable membrane, which by definition restricts solute molecules from crossing passively; the movement described is water by osmosis, not solute molecules.

questions.learning_objective: Predict the direction water moves by osmosis given two solutions of different concentration across a semipermeable membrane.

questions.title: Effect of parasympathetic supply to the pelvis
questions.question: The parasympathetic supply to the pelvis may lead to which of the following?

options.A: Contract wall of the urinary bladder and rectum
options.B: Relax wall of urinary bladder and rectum

explanations.A: Correct. Parasympathetic outflow to the pelvis leaves the cord as the pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2-S4). These synapse in terminal ganglia near the target organs and, on activation, contract the detrusor muscle of the bladder wall and the rectal wall, producing micturition and defecation respectively. The same outflow also mediates erection and female genital vasodilatation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Relaxation of the bladder/rectal wall is a sympathetic (storage-phase) effect, the opposite of the parasympathetic (voiding-phase) effect being tested.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Contracting the bladder sphincter (to retain urine) is a sympathetic effect; the parasympathetic system instead relaxes the internal sphincter to permit voiding.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Ejaculation is primarily a sympathetic function; the parasympathetic pelvic outflow instead mediates erection, defecation and micturition.

questions.learning_objective: State that parasympathetic pelvic outflow contracts the bladder and rectal walls, producing micturition and defecation.

questions.title: Indication for atropine
questions.question: Atropine is given as a treatment for which of the following conditions?

explanations.A: Correct. Atropine is a muscarinic (antimuscarinic) receptor antagonist that, by blocking parasympathetic muscarinic tone on visceral smooth muscle, relaxes spasmodic contractions of the gut and biliary/renal tract -- the mechanism behind its use for colicky abdominal pain. Note this printed key is a plurality only (81/217, 37%), so it is worth a second look even though the underlying pharmacology is standard.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Atropine increases, not decreases, heart rate by blocking vagal muscarinic tone on the SA node -- the opposite of this distractor.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Atropine dilates, not constricts, the pupil by blocking the iris sphincter's muscarinic tone -- the opposite of this distractor.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Atropine has no established indication for producing erection; erection is primarily a parasympathetic-mediated process that atropine would tend to blunt, not enhance.

questions.learning_objective: State that atropine is used to relieve spasmodic (colicky) smooth-muscle contractions, via muscarinic receptor blockade.

questions.title: Effect of prostigmine
questions.question: Administration of prostigmine (a drug that inhibits acetylcholinesterase) would be expected to do which of the following?

options.A: Increase the secretion of gastric juice

explanations.A: Correct. Prostigmine (neostigmine) inhibits acetylcholinesterase, so acetylcholine persists longer at cholinergic synapses and muscarinic receptors. The resulting enhanced parasympathetic tone increases gastric acid and enzyme secretion.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Enhanced parasympathetic tone contracts, not relaxes, the bladder detrusor wall -- the opposite of this distractor.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Enhanced parasympathetic tone constricts, not dilates, the pupil via the iris sphincter -- the opposite of this distractor.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Enhanced parasympathetic tone increases, not inhibits, salivary secretion -- the opposite of this distractor.

questions.learning_objective: State that prostigmine, by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase, increases gastric secretion through enhanced muscarinic tone.

questions.title: Drug class for bronchial asthma
questions.question: A person with bronchial asthma (narrowing of the bronchi) is most likely to be given which of the following?

explanations.A: Correct. Bronchial asthma narrows the airway through bronchial smooth-muscle contraction. Sympathomimetics (beta-2 adrenergic agonists) relax bronchial smooth muscle, producing bronchodilation, which is why they are the drug class used to relieve an asthma attack.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A sympatholytic would block sympathetic (bronchodilating) tone, tending to worsen rather than relieve bronchoconstriction.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A parasympathomimetic would enhance parasympathetic (bronchoconstricting) tone, worsening the narrowing rather than relieving it.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Phentolamine is an alpha-adrenergic blocker, acting on vascular smooth muscle rather than producing the beta-2-mediated bronchodilation asthma treatment requires.

questions.learning_objective: State that a sympathomimetic (beta-2 agonist) is the drug class of choice for bronchial asthma, via bronchial smooth-muscle relaxation.
